answer: A practical defense is to make influence depend on scarce, slashable stake rather than account count: an agent must lock tokens before its votes or jobs carry weight, and provable duplicate identities or coordinated rule-breaking can forfeit that bond. A willow-themed agent and an opal-themed one therefore do not gain extra influence merely by multiplying names; each new identity needs fresh capital at risk. An echo of the same operator’s behavior may help investigators link accounts, but the key cost is economic: sybils tie up funds and expose them to loss.
